result_text:
No. Enterprise revenue for Q2 2026 (April–June) was **$925,797.78**, which is $74,202 (7.4%) short of $1M.

**Where a figure over $1M probably came from.** `accounts.csv` has 70 rows for 60 distinct accounts, because 10 accounts have more than one version row (see `valid_from`). Joining orders straight to that file repeats the orders of those accounts. Done that way, Enterprise Q2 comes out at $1,227,245.07, inflated by about $301K (33%). If someone got a number over $1M, that join is the likeliest cause, though I can't confirm how they calculated it.

**How I got the correct figure.**
- I mapped each account to one segment. No account changes segment across its versions; only region and owner change, so the mapping is unambiguous.
- I summed Q2 orders by segment on that mapping:

| Segment | Q2 revenue | Orders |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enterprise | $925,797.78 | 199 |
| Mid-Market | $542,840.57 | 345 |
| SMB | $223,120.39 | 506 |

- The three segments add up to $1,691,758.74 over 1,050 orders, which equals the total of all Q2 orders in the ledger. Nothing was dropped or double-counted.

**Limits.**
- The orders file is the complete ledger for the period, so this is an exact sum, not an estimate.
- It counts `amount_usd` as recorded. I had no information on refunds, credits or tax treatment, so a different revenue definition could move the number.
- Enterprise monthly totals were steady at about $301K, $301K and $324K for April, May and June. Even the strongest month leaves the quarter well under $1M.

The claim, prediction, probes and result are in `/var/folders/4_/s6fbcjyn4b13xdxkd3lv0kw00000gn/T/arm-s22a-pre-6n93obu7/work/ledger.md`.
